A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniCode research. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and Appendices A–B support reliable comparison despite rewriting and pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations, test-generation ablations, recursive-augmentation experiments, and an expert assessment of 113 generated problems.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds mixed-generator evaluation results, a targeted problem-validity audit, and correlated-failure findings.

M1.justification: The five augmentation axes and the three-stage brute-force filtering, majority-voting, and LLM-adjudication pipeline remain unchanged. Clarified generator roles and expanded explanations do not establish a different proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds actual evaluation of UniCode-Multi, previously described as a future release. Its five-generator mixture extends evaluated problem sources beyond the separate o4-mini and DeepSeek-R1 sets to include GPT-5-, Gemini-, and Qwen-generated problems, within the same competitive-programming task.

E2.justification: The model roster in Table 1, existing model comparisons in Table 5, and rStar-Coder comparison in Table 3 are retained. The added mixed-generator column evaluates existing models; newly cited research is not introduced as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 adds a targeted audit of 115 problems that all models failed, reporting nine exclusions. Appendix B.3 adds evaluation on a five-generator mixture. These introduce reported selection and evaluation procedures; the PDFs do not establish reruns or explain how the exclusions relate to the unchanged leaderboard.

E4.justification: v3 extends generator-bias analysis with mixed-source results, adds an audit testing whether universally failed problems are invalid, and reports correlated-failure analysis for brute-force filtering in B.1. Existing component ablations, sensitivity sweeps, recursive augmentation, and error case studies remain.

E5.justification: Correlation and p-value reporting, expert-agreement reporting, and Appendix B.5's confidence intervals and error-bound treatment are retained. No additional repeated-run, random-seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds five mixed-generator scores, including GPT-5 at 68.8%, and changes o3-mini's existing o4-mini-generated-set score from 57.1% to 55.1%. B.3 corrects DeepSeek-R1's corresponding prose value from 55.6% to 56.6%. Newly reported findings include correlated failures falling from 18.7% to 5.2% under filtering, nine invalid audited problems, and $0.041 generation cost per problem. Table 1 is unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, resource-limit formulas, Appendix B.5 derivations and bounds, and B.6 capacity calculations are unchanged. The corrected complexity example in the error-analysis prompt does not introduce new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The framework's three contributions, 31.2% performance-collapse claim, and seed-problem regression claim remain. Section 1 strengthens the diagnostic contribution from categorizing failures to explicitly claiming that error decomposition separates intrinsic reasoning or implementation failures from memorization-induced bias.

C2.justification: A new limitations section identifies difficulties verifying complex compositional tasks and the risk of models overfitting to UniCode's generation pipeline. B.1 adds an explanation linking exhaustive brute-force search to reduced shared logical failures, while B.3 interprets the mixed-generator results as smoothing stylistic bias.

D1.justification: v3 adds a public evaluation-code access statement, discloses selection of 600 seeds across 15 algorithms, clarifies generator/adjudicator roles, and reports generation cost. Conversely, B.3 drops v2's proposed composition of 100 problems per generator without specifying the evaluated mixture's size. Repository availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: Section 6 substantially revises research positioning: it removes the open-ended-search and agent-benchmark discussion, integrates test generation into generative evaluation, and adds a dedicated reasoning-versus-memorization discussion. New references include Wu et al. (2024), Hazra et al. (2025), and von Recum et al. (2026), alongside a new connection to AlphaEvolve.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. v3 adds limitations and acknowledgements, reorganizes related-work subsections, renames the ethics statement and B.4, updates author and conference information, and makes numerous language corrections.

P2.justification: Table 5 gains a mixed-generator column and revised caption. Figure 4 moves between columns, Figures 1–2 receive caption edits, and blue hyperlinks and text reflow alter presentation. The scientific figure artwork and other table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency through code-access information and explicit limitations, while the targeted validity audit and mixed-generator results strengthen documented validation. The gains are limited: the mixed-set size is unspecified, the audit's relationship to the unchanged leaderboard is unclear, and the new correlated-failure rates lack detailed methodological support.
